newsitem.title: GERMANY: GERMAN FIRMS SWITCH TO UPS RIVALS FOR US DELIVERY.
newsitem.headline: GERMAN FIRMS SWITCH TO UPS RIVALS FOR US DELIVERY.

text.p: Some German exporters are switching goods away from strike-hit United Parcel Service of America Inc to ensure delivery in the U.S., competitor transport companies said.
DHL International, Federal Express Inc. and TNT all reported a upturn in air shipments from Germany to the U.S. this week but declined to give precise figures.
DHL has placed prominent adverts in German newspapers encouraging firms "experiencing difficulties at present with U.S. deliveries" to use its overnight service.
A DHL spokesman told Reuters:"We have had many enquiries and there is an increase in business, although I cannot say just how much."
But the firm had no plans at present for additional air capacity or extra staff to handle the new business, he added.
A FedEx spokesman said: "We have a slight increase in volumes. Our existing customers have priority but we are trying to satisfy all the new customers as well."
FedEx had contingency plans should the additional shipments increase substantially, he added without releasing more details.
A TNT spokesman said: "German companies are seeking alternatives to make sure their exports to the U.S. are delivered.
"We have a clear increase in shipments to the U.S. although it is unclear whether this is from the UPS strike or general growth," he added.
In London a DHL spokeswoman said there: " was a steady trickle of enquiries and new business for the U.S. but not the strong demand which might have been expected."
